IDEA: Measure whether open-weight LLMs exhibit conditional topical concentration in scientific idea generation — producing lower inter-sample topic entropy than human experts performing the same task — and calibrate whether this concentration correlates with expert-judged novelty loss.

BACKGROUND: Claims that LLMs suffer "mode collapse" in scientific ideation typically compare conditional LLM outputs to unconditional field-publication marginals, conflating task-conditioning effects with genuine distributional narrowing, and proxying training data with unrelated web corpora for closed models. It remains unresolved whether, under matched task-conditioning and matched register, LLMs produce topically narrower idea pools than human experts, and whether any such narrowing has measurable consequences for idea novelty or quality.

APPROACH: We restrict the study to fully open models with known training data — OLMo-7B, Pythia-12B, and LLM360-Amber — so the training-topic prior p_train can be computed directly from Dolma (OLMo), The Pile (Pythia), and the LLM360 release. For each model we generate 10,000 ideas across 20 arXiv fields at 5 decoding temperatures (0.3–1.3) with 3 prompt paraphrases, and compare against two human-expert sets (10K NSF 2019–2023 abstracts, 10K NeurIPS/ACL/ICML 2020–2024 abstracts), all length- and register-normalized via a fixed rewrite-to-idea-statement prompt applied uniformly to every source (including a human-abstract→LLM-register style-transfer control). Topics are assigned via a jointly-fit BERTopic model and a SPECTER2+mini-batch-k-means model at K∈{50,500,2000}; per source we compute Shannon entropy, Good-Turing–corrected entropy, topic coverage, KL to p_train, Self-BLEU, and embedding dispersion, plus a sanity check that two disjoint NSF halves show no entropy gap under the pipeline.

EXPERIMENT: The primary falsification test is a permutation test on H(p_LLM) vs. H(p_human) under identical task-conditioning and register, pre-registered to require a significant entropy deficit in ≥2 of 3 open models with non-overlapping bootstrap CIs and stability across all K, embedding, and seed choices; a matched subsample of 2,000 ideas (LLM + human) is rated by domain experts on novelty and feasibility (blinded, 1–5 Likert), and we pre-register that the topical-concentration claim is only scientifically meaningful if lower entropy correlates with lower expert novelty ratings (Spearman ρ < −0.2, p<0.05). Effect-size thresholds for entropy gaps are derived post hoc from the human-rating calibration rather than fixed a priori.
